blocks.original_text:
- name: int_qualtrics__contacts
      description: XM Directory contacts joined with mailing list aggregates and flags; one row per directory_id + contact_id
      grain: One row per directory_id + contact_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_contact
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__contact_mailing_list_membership
      business_logic: '- Start from all rows in staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_contact. - From staging.stg_qualtrics__contact_mailing_list_membership, for each (directory_id, contact_id): - Count distinct mailing_list_id into two metrics: - count_mailing_lists_subscribed_to counts lists where is_unsubscribed = false. - count_mailing_lists_unsubscribed_from counts lists where is_unsubscribed = true. - Rows with is_unsubscribed = NULL do not contribute; NULL mailing_list_id are excluded. If membership rows exist but none match a condition, the corresponding count is 0. - Concatenate all mailing_list_id values with the delimiter ", " across all membership rows; NULL mailing_list_id are excluded; duplicates are preserved; order is not guaranteed. Result is NULL if no non-NULL mailing_list_id exist for the contact in the directory. - Left join these aggregates to directory_contact on (directory_id, contact_id). - Output: - Set is_xm_directory_contact = true and is_research_core_contact = false for all rows. - Rename ext_ref to external_data_reference; all other selected fields are passed through from directory_contact. - If a contact has no membership rows in a directory, mailing_list_ids and both count fields are NULL due to the left join.'
      columns:
      - name: contact_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact identifier within the directory; pairs with directory_id to define the row
      - name: is_xm_directory_contact
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Constant true for all rows
      - name: is_research_core_contact
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Constant false for all rows
      - name: directory_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Directory identifier; used to join aggregates and define the grain with contact_id
      - name: email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pass-through email from directory_contact; nullable
      - name: email_domain
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pass-through email domain from directory_contact; nullable
      - name: first_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pass-through first name from directory_contact; nullable
      - name: last_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pass-through last name from directory_contact; nullable
      - name: external_data_reference
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pass-through of ext_ref from directory_contact (renamed); nullable
      - name: language
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pass-through language from directory_contact; nullable
      - name: is_unsubscribed_from_directory
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Directory-level unsubscribe flag from directory_contact; pass-through
      - name: unsubscribed_from_directory_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Directory-level unsubscribe timestamp from directory_contact; pass-through; nullable
      - name: last_modified_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Last modification timestamp from directory_contact; pass-through; nullable
      - name: mailing_list_ids
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma+space concatenation of mailing_list_id per directory_id+contact_id; NULL ids excluded; duplicates preserved; order not guaranteed; NULL if no non-NULL mailing_list_id
      - name: count_mailing_lists_subscribed_to
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of mailing_list_id where is_unsubscribed=false per directory_id+contact_id; excludes NULL ids and NULL status; NULL if no membership rows; 0 if memberships exist but none match
      - name: count_mailing_lists_unsubscribed_from
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of mailing_list_id where is_unsubscribed=true per directory_id+contact_id; excludes NULL ids and NULL status; NULL if no membership rows; 0 if memberships exist but none match
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Contact creation timestamp from directory_contact; pass-through; nullable

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_qualtrics__question
      description: Intermediate Qualtrics question rows enriched with sub-question and block metadata; one row per question–sub-question–block combination
      grain: One row per combination of survey_id, question_id, sub_question_key, and block_id (NULLs possible due to left joins)
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__question
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__sub_question
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__block_question
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__block
      business_logic: '- Start from all rows in staging.stg_qualtrics__question (alias question); no filters are applied. - Derive parent_question_id by splitting question_id on delimiter "#" and taking the first segment; if "#" is absent, parent_question_id equals question_id; if question_id starts with "#", the result is an empty string; if question_id is NULL, parent_question_id is NULL; casing and whitespace are preserved. - Left join staging.stg_qualtrics__sub_question on (survey_id, question_id) to bring key→sub_question_key, text→sub_question_text, and choice_data_export_tag; if no match, these fields are NULL; multiple sub_question matches fan out rows. - Left join staging.stg_qualtrics__block_question on (survey_id, question_id) to attach block_id; if no match, block_id is NULL; if multiple matches, rows multiply further. - Left join staging.stg_qualtrics__block on (block_question.block_id = block.block_id AND block_question.survey_id = block.survey_id) to bring block metadata: description→block_description, randomize_questions→block_question_randomization, type→block_type, block_visibility, is_locked→is_block_locked; if no block match, these fields are NULL. - Select and pass through question-level attributes (text, selectors, flags, validation settings, export tags, next_* fields) without trimming, case normalization, casting, or aggregation. - No DISTINCT, ordering, or de-duplication is performed; duplicates produced by joins are preserved; NULLs propagate from left joins.'
      columns:
      - name: question_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary question identifier from stg_qualtrics__question; join key; duplicates may occur due to downstream fan-out
      - name: parent_question_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Substring of question_id before the first '#'; if no '#', equals question_id; may be empty if question_id starts with '#'; NULL when question_id is NULL; casing/whitespace preserved
      - name: question_text
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Question text passthrough from stg_qualtrics__question.question_text; no normalization
      - name: survey_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey identifier passthrough used for all joins; no normalization
      - name: question_description
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__question.question_description; may be NULL
      - name: question_description_option
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__question.question_description_option; may be NULL
      - name: sub_question_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__sub_question.key; NULL when no matching sub_question; duplicates preserved
      - name: sub_question_text
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__sub_question.text; NULL when no matching sub_question
      - name: question_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__question.question_type; may be NULL
      - name: selector
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__question.selector; may be NULL
      - name: sub_selector
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__question.sub_selector; may be NULL
      - name: is_data_hidden
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Passthrough flag from stg_qualtrics__question.is_data_hidden; TRUE/FALSE or NULL
      - name: is_data_private
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Passthrough flag from stg_qualtrics__question.is_data_private; TRUE/FALSE or NULL
      - name: validation_setting_force_response
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Passthrough numeric from stg_qualtrics__question.validation_setting_force_response; NULLable
      - name: validation_setting_force_response_type
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Passthrough numeric from stg_qualtrics__question.validation_setting_force_response_type; NULLable
      - name: validation_setting_type
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Passthrough numeric from stg_qualtrics__question.validation_setting_type; NULLable
      - name: data_export_tag

        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__question.data_export_tag; may be NULL
      - name: choice_data_export_tag
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__sub_question.choice_data_export_tag; NULL when no matching sub_question
      - name: block_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Block identifier from stg_qualtrics__block_question.block_id; NULL when no matching block_question
      - name: block_description
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__block.description; NULL when no matching block
      - name: block_question_randomization
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Passthrough numeric from stg_qualtrics__block.randomize_questions; NULL when no matching block
      - name: block_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Passthrough from stg_qualtrics__block.type; NULL when no matching block
      - name: block_visibility
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Passthrough numeric from stg_qualtrics__block.block_visibility; NULL when no matching block
      - name: is_block_locked
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Passthrough flag from stg_qualtrics__block.is_locked; TRUE/FALSE or NULL when no matching block
      - name: next_answer_id
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Passthrough flag from stg_qualtrics__question.next_answer_id; TRUE/FALSE or NULL
      - name: next_choice_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Passthrough integer from stg_qualtrics__question.next_choice_id; may be NULL

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_qualtrics__response_quality
      description: 'Per-response quality metrics computed from Qualtrics staging data: timing category, overall rating, numeric score, analysis inclusion flag, and run timestamp'
      grain: One row per staging survey response with non-null duration_in_seconds and progress
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
      business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response using fields: response_id, survey_id, duration_in_seconds, progress, is_finished. - Filter out rows where duration_in_seconds OR progress is NULL; no other filtering, joins, ordering, or deduplication is applied. - Compute timing_quality from duration_in_seconds using inclusive thresholds where stated: - "Too Fast" if duration_in_seconds < 30 - "Too Slow" if duration_in_seconds > 3600 - "Optimal" if duration_in_seconds between 120 and 1800 inclusive - "Suboptimal" otherwise (covers 30–119 and 1801–3600, inclusive of 30 and 3600) - Compute overall_quality_rating with ordered precedence (first match wins): - "High Quality" if is_finished is true AND progress >= 0.95 AND duration_in_seconds between 60 and 3600 inclusive - "Good Quality" if is_finished is true AND progress >= 0.8 - "Fair Quality" if progress >= 0.5 - "Poor Quality" otherwise Note: is_finished NULL does not satisfy the true condition (no coercion). - Compute quality_score with the same conditions and precedence as overall_quality_rating: - 90 for "High Quality", 75 for "Good Quality", 60 for "Fair Quality", 30 for "Poor Quality". - Set include_in_analysis = true only if is_finished is true AND progress >= 0.8 AND duration_in_seconds between 30 and 7200 inclusive; else false. - Set analysis_date to the execution time using the environment’s current timestamp; same value for all rows in a run. - Output the original fields plus the derived fields; no aggregations, and duplicate response_id values (if present in staging) are preserved.'
      columns:
      - name: response_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Identifier of the survey response from staging; may repeat if the source contains duplicates
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: survey_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Identifier of the survey to which the response belongs (passed through from staging; may be NULL)
      - name: duration_in_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Response duration in seconds from staging; non-null due to filter; used for threshold comparisons only
      - name: progress
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completion fraction from staging; non-null due to filter; compared against 0.5, 0.8, and 0.95 thresholds
      - name: is_finished
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Staging completion flag; may be NULL; NULL does not satisfy true in condition checks
      - name: timing_quality
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Timing category from duration_in_seconds: ''Too Fast''(<30), ''Too Slow''(>3600), ''Optimal''(120–1800 inclusive), else ''Suboptimal'''
      - name: overall_quality_rating
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Ordered evaluation: High if finished and progress>=0.95 and duration 60–3600; else Good if finished and progress>=0.8; else Fair if progress>=0.5; else Poor'
      - name: quality_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Score mapped from rating rules: 90 (High), 75 (Good), 60 (Fair), 30 (Poor)'
      - name: include_in_analysis
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: True only if finished and progress>=0.8 and duration_in_seconds between 30 and 7200 inclusive; otherwise false
      - name: analysis_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution timestamp assigned to all rows in the run using the environment’s current timestamp

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_qualtrics__survey
      description: Survey records enriched with published version metadata, counts of previously published versions, and related user emails.
      grain: One row per survey_id per published survey_version row
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_version
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__user
      business_logic: '- Load all survey fields from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey unchanged; NULLs, casing, and whitespace are preserved. - Load all survey_version records from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_version. - Define latest_version as the set of survey_version records flagged as published; no tie-breaking or deduplication is applied. - For agg_versions, for each survey_id count unique version_number values among survey_version records flagged as previously published; missing version_number values are ignored. - Load users from staging.stg_qualtrics__user to resolve emails by user_id. - Left join survey to latest_version on survey_id. - Left join users three times: - version_publisher on publisher_user_id to obtain publisher_email, - owner on owner_user_id to obtain owner_email, - creator on creator_user_id to obtain creator_email. - Left join agg_versions on survey_id. - Output survey.* plus: version_id, version_number, version_description, survey_version_created_at (from the published survey_version created_at), count_published_versions, publisher_user_id, publisher_email, creator_email, owner_email. - Null and duplication behavior: - Left joins preserve survey rows; if no match, joined fields are NULL. - No ordering or deduplication is performed; if multiple published versions exist for a survey, one row is produced per matching version. If the user table contains multiple rows per user_id, additional duplicate combinations may appear.'

      - name: survey_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique survey identifier used to join to versions and users.
      - name: survey_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Human-readable survey name from the survey record.
      - name: survey_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Lifecycle status of the survey from the survey record.
      - name: brand_base_url
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Base URL for the Qualtrics brand associated with the survey.
      - name: brand_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Qualtrics brand identifier associated with the survey.
      - name: bundle_short_name
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Bundle short name value from the survey record; numeric and may be NULL.
      - name: composition_type
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Composition type value from the survey record; numeric and may be NULL.
      - name: auto_scoring_category
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Auto scoring category setting from the survey record; numeric and may be NULL.
      - name: default_scoring_category
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Default scoring category setting from the survey record; numeric and may be NULL.
      - name: division_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Division identifier associated with the survey; integer and may be NULL.

- name: int_qualtrics__survey_embedded_data
      description: Aggregates embedded key/value pairs per response into a single JSON-like string.
      grain: One row per response_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_embedded_data
      business_logic: '- Read rows from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_embedded_data using fields response_id, key, value. - Group records by response_id. - For each response_id, build embedded_data by concatenating all non-null "key:value" pairs with ", " as the separator, then wrap the result with leading "{" and trailing "}". - Pair order is not specified; original casing and whitespace are preserved; there is no quoting or escaping; duplicate pairs are kept. - If key or value is NULL, that pair is excluded; if all pairs are excluded, embedded_data is NULL (no braces). - Finally, retain unique combinations of response_id and embedded_data; because embedded_data is already constructed per response_id, the result remains one row per response_id.'
      columns:
      - name: response_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey response identifier used for grouping; exactly one output row per response_id; may be NULL.
      - name: embedded_data
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: JSON-like string of 'key:value' pairs wrapped in braces and separated by ', '; pair order unspecified; duplicates preserved; pairs with NULL key or value are excluded; if none remain, this field is NULL; casing and whitespace are preserved with no quoting or escaping.

- name: int_qualtrics__survey_performance
      description: Simplified per-survey response metrics (counts, averages, completion rate) with execution timestamp
      grain: One row per survey_id with at least one distinct response_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
      business_logic: '- Load survey_id, survey_name, and survey_status from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey. - From staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response, exclude responses with NULL survey_id and aggregate by survey_id: - total_responses: count of unique response_id. - completed_responses: count of unique response_id where is_finished is true. - avg_completion_rate: average of progress; NULL values are ignored. - avg_completion_time_seconds: average of duration_in_seconds (in seconds); NULL values are ignored. - Left join these aggregates to the survey base on survey_id. - Replace missing aggregates with 0. - Set completion_rate to completed_responses divided by total_responses when total_responses > 0; otherwise 0. - Set analysis_date to the current timestamp at run time. - Keep only surveys with total_responses greater than 0.'
      columns:
      - name: survey_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique survey identifier; one row per survey_id with at least one response
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: survey_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey name from the survey source
      - name: survey_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey status from the survey source
      - name: total_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of unique response_id per survey_id; responses with NULL survey_id excluded; always > 0 due to final filter
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: completed_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of unique finished response_id per survey_id; bounded between 0 and total_responses
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: avg_completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average progress across responses; NULL progress ignored; 0 if all progress values are NULL
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: avg_completion_time_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average duration_in_seconds across responses; NULL durations ignored; 0 if all durations are NULL
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Ratio of completed_responses to total_responses when total_responses > 0; else 0; value between 0 and 1
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: analysis_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp set to the current time when the model runs
        tests:
        - not_null

- name: int_qualtrics__user_engagement
      description: Aggregated Qualtrics response metrics per user with engagement labels and scores
      grain: One row per user_identifier with at least one response where recorded_date is not null
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
      business_logic: '- Input filtering: only survey_response rows with recorded_date present are used. - User identifier: use recipient_email when available; otherwise use the literal prefix "anonymous_" followed by response_id. Casing and spacing from source are preserved. The output includes only users with at least one non-null response_id, so identifiers are present. - Group by user_identifier and compute: - total_responses: number of unique response_id values; missing IDs are ignored. - completed_responses: number of unique response_id values where the response is marked finished; missing IDs are ignored. - surveys_participated: number of unique survey_id values; missing survey IDs are ignored. - avg_completion_progress: average of progress values; missing values are ignored; returns NULL if none exist. - avg_response_duration: average of duration_in_seconds (in seconds); missing values are ignored; returns NULL if none exist. - completion_rate_score: if total_responses > 0, compute completed_responses / total_responses * 100; otherwise 0. No explicit rounding is applied. - engagement_level: based on total_responses thresholds: 10 or more → High Engagement; 5–9 → Medium Engagement; 2–4 → Low Engagement; 1 → Single Response. - overall_engagement_score: 5 points per response plus 10 points per completed response, capped at 100. - analysis_date: set to the current timestamp at model execution; identical across rows within a run. - Final filter: keep only users where total_responses > 0.'
      columns:
      - name: user_identifier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Recipient email if present; otherwise 'anonymous_' plus response_id; one row per identifier; non-null in output
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: total_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique response_id values for the user; missing IDs ignored; strictly greater than zero
      - name: completed_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique response_id values marked finished for the user; missing IDs ignored
      - name: surveys_participated
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique survey_id values associated with the user; missing values ignored
      - name: avg_completion_progress
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of progress values across the user's responses; ignores missing; returns NULL if none
      - name: avg_response_duration
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of duration_in_seconds across the user's responses; ignores missing; unit is seconds; returns NULL if none
      - name: engagement_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Label by total_responses: High (>=10), Medium (>=5), Low (>=2), else Single Response'
      - name: completion_rate_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completion percentage computed as completed_responses divided by total_responses times 100; 0–100; unrounded
      - name: overall_engagement_score
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Score equals 5 per response plus 10 per completed response, capped at 100
      - name: analysis_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Current timestamp at model execution; identical across rows in a run; time zone preserved

The output includes only users with at least one non-null response_id, so identifiers are present. - Group by user_identifier and compute: - total_responses: number of unique response_id values; missing IDs are ignored. - completed_responses: number of unique response_id values where the response is marked finished; missing IDs are ignored. - surveys_participated: number of unique survey_id values; missing survey IDs are ignored. - avg_completion_progress: average of progress values; missing values are ignored; returns NULL if none exist. - avg_response_duration: average of duration_in_seconds (in seconds); missing values are ignored; returns NULL if none exist. - completion_rate_score: if total_responses > 0, compute completed_responses / total_responses * 100; otherwise 0. No explicit rounding is applied. - engagement_level: based on total_responses thresholds: 10 or more → High Engagement; 5–9 → Medium Engagement; 2–4 → Low Engagement; 1 → Single Response. - overall_engagement_score: 5 points per response plus 10 points per completed response, capped at 100. - analysis_date: set to the current timestamp at model execution; identical across rows within a run. - Final filter: keep only users where total_responses > 0.'

      description: Channel-level performance metrics, market share, ranks, tiering, and recommendations computed from Qualtrics survey responses
      grain: One row per non-null distribution_channel with at least one non-null response_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
      business_logic: '- Read all records from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response (fields used: distribution_channel, survey_id, response_id, is_finished, recipient_email, progress, duration_in_seconds). - Exclude rows where distribution_channel is NULL. - For each distribution_channel, compute: - surveys_using_channel: number of unique survey_id values (NULL survey_id ignored). - total_responses: number of unique response_id values (NULL response_id ignored). - completed_responses: number of unique response_id values where is_finished is true. - unique_participants: number of unique participant identifiers using recipient_email, defaulting to ''anonymous_'' + response_id when email is NULL; NULL outcomes are not counted. - completion_rate: completed_responses divided by total_responses; if total_responses is 0, set to 0. - avg_progress: arithmetic mean of progress, ignoring NULL values. - avg_duration: arithmetic mean of duration_in_seconds (seconds), ignoring NULL values. - rushed_responses: number of unique response_id values where duration_in_seconds < 60. - lengthy_responses: number of unique response_id values where duration_in_seconds > 3600. - efficiency_score: if total_responses > 0 and avg_duration > 0, compute completion_rate × duration_factor × 100, where duration_factor is 1.0 when avg_duration is between 120 and 1800 seconds inclusive, otherwise 0.8; else 0. - Across all channels (no partition), compute: - market_share: total_responses divided by the sum of total_responses across all channels. - completion_rank: rank by completion_rate descending (ties share ranks with gaps). - efficiency_rank: rank by efficiency_score descending (ties share ranks with gaps). - Classify: - channel_tier: Tier 1 - Premium when completion_rate ≥ 0.8 and efficiency_score ≥ 80; Tier 2 - Strong when completion_rate ≥ 0.6 and efficiency_score ≥ 60; Tier 3 - Average when completion_rate ≥ 0.4; otherwise Tier 4 - Underperforming. - strategic_recommendation: Scale and optimize when completion_rate ≥ 0.7 and market_share ≥ 0.2; Invest for growth when completion_rate ≥ 0.6 and market_share < 0.1; Improve or consider replacement when completion_rate < 0.4; otherwise Monitor and maintain. - Set analysis_date to the current timestamp at query execution. - Return only channels with total_responses > 0 and order rows by efficiency_score descending, then market_share descending.'
      columns:
      - name: distribution_channel
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Channel identifier used for grouping; non-null; exactly one row per value
        tests:
        - not_null

        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique survey_id count within the channel; NULL survey_id ignored
      - name: total_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique response_id count within the channel; NULL response_id ignored
      - name: completed_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique response_id count where is_finished is true; NULL response_id ignored
      - name: unique_participants
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique count using recipient_email, falling back to 'anonymous_' + response_id when email is NULL; NULL outcomes not counted; original casing preserved
      - name: completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Ratio of completed_responses to total_responses when total_responses > 0, else 0; no rounding
      - name: avg_progress
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean of progress for the channel; NULL values ignored; no rounding
      - name: avg_duration
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean of duration_in_seconds in seconds; NULL values ignored; no rounding
      - name: rushed_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique response_id count where duration_in_seconds < 60; NULL durations ignored
      - name: lengthy_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique response_id count where duration_in_seconds > 3600; NULL durations ignored
      - name: efficiency_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: If total_responses > 0 and avg_duration > 0, completion_rate × duration_factor × 100 where duration_factor is 1.0 for 120–1800 seconds inclusive, else 0.8; otherwise 0; no rounding
      - name: market_share
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Channel total_responses divided by the sum across all channels; computed before final filtering; no rounding
      - name: completion_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Rank across all channels by completion_rate descending; ties share ranks with gaps; computed before final filtering
      - name: efficiency_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Rank across all channels by efficiency_score descending; ties share ranks with gaps; computed before final filtering
      - name: channel_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Tier 1 if completion_rate ≥ 0.8 and efficiency_score ≥ 80; Tier 2 if completion_rate ≥ 0.6 and efficiency_score ≥ 60; Tier 3 if completion_rate ≥ 0.4; else Tier 4
      - name: strategic_recommendation
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Scale and optimize if completion_rate ≥ 0.7 and market_share ≥ 0.2; Invest for growth if completion_rate ≥ 0.6 and market_share < 0.1; Improve or consider replacement if completion_rate < 0.4; else Monitor and maintain
      - name: analysis_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp at query execution; identical across output rows; time zone preserved

blocks.original_text:
- name: qualtrics__contact
      description: Contact profile with directory attributes and aggregated survey engagement metrics
      grain: One row per contact_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__contacts
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__directory
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution_contact
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
      business_logic: '- Use intermediate.int_qualtrics__contacts as the base; one output row per contacts.contact_id. - Build distribution_response by: - Joining distribution_contact to distribution on distribution_id to add survey_id. - Left joining survey_response on both response_id and survey_id to add distribution_channel, progress, duration_in_seconds, is_finished, recorded_date; retain sent_at, opened_at, response_started_at, response_completed_at from distribution_contact. - For each contact_id, compute channel-specific counts as the number of distinct survey_id meeting each condition; survey_id must be present, and counts default to 0 when no matches: - Sent via email: sent_at present and distribution_channel is "email". - Sent via SMS: sent_at present and distribution_channel is "smsinvite". - Opened via email: opened_at present and distribution_channel is "email". - Opened via SMS: opened_at present and distribution_channel is "smsinvite". - Started via email: response_started_at present and distribution_channel is "email". - Started via SMS: response_started_at present and distribution_channel is "smsinvite". - Completed via email: response_completed_at present and distribution_channel is "email". - Completed via SMS: response_completed_at present and distribution_channel is "smsinvite". - For each contact_id, compute overall survey engagement across all distribution_response rows: - total_count_surveys: distinct survey_id across all rows; defaults to 0 when none. - total_count_completed_surveys: distinct survey_id where is_finished is true; defaults to 0 when none. - avg_survey_progress_pct: average of progress over non-NULL values; NULL when no non-NULL inputs. - avg_survey_duration_in_seconds: average of duration_in_seconds over non-NULL values; NULL when no non-NULL inputs. - last_survey_response_recorded_at: the latest recorded_date; NULL when none. - first_survey_response_recorded_at: the earliest recorded_date; NULL when none. - Compute medians per contact_id over non-NULL values using the 50th percentile with continuous interpolation: - median_survey_duration_in_seconds from duration_in_seconds. - median_survey_progress_pct from progress. - Join directory by contacts.directory_id to bring directory_name (name) and is_in_default_directory (is_default). - Final output includes all contact fields plus the computed aggregates and directory attributes; all joins are left joins to maintain one row per contact_id.'

references.name: intermediate.int_qualtrics__contacts
references.line_text: business_logic: '- Use intermediate.int_qualtrics__contacts as the base; one output row per contacts.contact_id. - Build distribution_response by: - Joining distribution_contact to distribution on distribution_id to add survey_id. - Left joining survey_response on both response_id and survey_id to add distribution_channel, progress, duration_in_seconds, is_finished, recorded_date; retain sent_at, opened_at, response_started_at, response_completed_at from distribution_contact. - For each contact_id, compute channel-specific counts as the number of distinct survey_id meeting each condition; survey_id must be present, and counts default to 0 when no matches: - Sent via email: sent_at present and distribution_channel is "email". - Sent via SMS: sent_at present and distribution_channel is "smsinvite". - Opened via email: opened_at present and distribution_channel is "email". - Opened via SMS: opened_at present and distribution_channel is "smsinvite". - Started via email: response_started_at present and distribution_channel is "email". - Started via SMS: response_started_at present and distribution_channel is "smsinvite". - Completed via email: response_completed_at present and distribution_channel is "email". - Completed via SMS: response_completed_at present and distribution_channel is "smsinvite". - For each contact_id, compute overall survey engagement across all distribution_response rows: - total_count_surveys: distinct survey_id across all rows; defaults to 0 when none. - total_count_completed_surveys: distinct survey_id where is_finished is true; defaults to 0 when none. - avg_survey_progress_pct: average of progress over non-NULL values; NULL when no non-NULL inputs. - avg_survey_duration_in_seconds: average of duration_in_seconds over non-NULL values; NULL when no non-NULL inputs. - last_survey_response_recorded_at: the latest recorded_date; NULL when none. - first_survey_response_recorded_at: the earliest recorded_date; NULL when none. - Compute medians per contact_id over non-NULL values using the 50th percentile with continuous interpolation: - median_survey_duration_in_seconds from duration_in_seconds. - median_survey_progress_pct from progress. - Join directory by contacts.directory_id to bring directory_name (name) and is_in_default_directory (is_default). - Final output includes all contact fields plus the computed aggregates and directory attributes; all joins are left joins to maintain one row per contact_id.'

source_comparison.scope: direct physical relation references through reachable local CTE/subqueries; no transitive expansion through other output tables or stored views

blocks.original_text:
- name: qualtrics__daily_breakdown
      description: Daily Qualtrics contact and response metrics with zero-filled counts per calendar day
      grain: One row per date_day
      source_models:
      - mart.qualtrics__response
      - mart.qualtrics__contact
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__contact_mailing_list_membership
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution_contact
      business_logic: '- Build a continuous daily date spine from the earliest survey send date to seven days after today; if no sends exist, start at 2016-01-01. Each spine entry is a midnight timestamp named date_day. - Aggregate responses by the calendar day of survey_response_recorded_at; records with an unparseable recorded timestamp are excluded. Compute: - Distinct surveys with at least one response that day. - Distinct responses that day, and distinct finished responses that day. - Channel-based distinct response counts using Qualtrics channel values: anonymous; social (reported as social_media); gl (reported as personal_link); qr (reported as qr_code); email; smsinvite (reported as sms). For each channel, also count finished responses. Uncategorized includes channels not in that list. - Aggregate distribution activity by the day the survey was sent: distinct contacts sent, opened, started, and completed. Opened/started/completed are attributed to the sent day (based on sent_at), not to their own event timestamps. - Aggregate contacts by day: distinct contacts created and distinct contacts unsubscribed from the directory. - Aggregate mailing list unsubscriptions by day: distinct contacts unsubscribed from a mailing list. - Left join all aggregates to the spine on date_day and replace missing counts with 0 to ensure one row per day.'
      columns:
      - name: date_day
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Midnight timestamp for the calendar day from the spine; one row per day
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: count_contacts_created
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct contacts created on this day; 0 if none
      - name: count_contacts_unsubscribed_from_directory
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct contacts that unsubscribed from the directory on this day; 0 if none
      - name: count_contacts_unsubscribed_from_mailing_list
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct contacts that unsubscribed from a mailing list on this day; 0 if none
      - name: count_contacts_sent_surveys
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct contacts with surveys sent on this day (based on sent_at); 0 if none
      - name: count_contacts_opened_sent_surveys
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct contacts who opened a sent survey, counted on the sent day; 0 if none
      - name: count_contacts_started_sent_surveys
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct contacts who started a sent survey, counted on the sent day; 0 if none
      - name: count_contacts_completed_sent_surveys
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct contacts who completed a sent survey, counted on the sent day; 0 if none
      - name: count_distinct_surveys_responded_to
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct surveys with at least one response recorded on this day; records with unparseable times are excluded; 0 if none
      - name: total_count_survey_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct responses recorded on this day; records with unparseable times are excluded; 0 if none
      - name: total_count_completed_survey_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct finished responses recorded on this day; 0 if none
      - name: count_anonymous_survey_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct responses recorded on this day from the anonymous channel; 0 if none
      - name: count_anonymous_completed_survey_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct finished responses recorded on this day from the anonymous channel; 0 if none
      - name: count_social_media_survey_responses

current_date + interval 7 days,

business_logic: '- Build a continuous daily date spine from the earliest survey send date to seven days after today; if no sends exist, start at 2016-01-01. Each spine entry is a midnight timestamp named date_day. - Aggregate responses by the calendar day of survey_response_recorded_at; records with an unparseable recorded timestamp are excluded. Compute: - Distinct surveys with at least one response that day. - Distinct responses that day, and distinct finished responses that day. - Channel-based distinct response counts using Qualtrics channel values: anonymous; social (reported as social_media); gl (reported as personal_link); qr (reported as qr_code); email; smsinvite (reported as sms). For each channel, also count finished responses. Uncategorized includes channels not in that list. - Aggregate distribution activity by the day the survey was sent: distinct contacts sent, opened, started, and completed. Opened/started/completed are attributed to the sent day (based on sent_at), not to their own event timestamps. - Aggregate contacts by day: distinct contacts created and distinct contacts unsubscribed from the directory. - Aggregate mailing list unsubscriptions by day: distinct contacts unsubscribed from a mailing list. - Left join all aggregates to the spine on date_day and replace missing counts with 0 to ensure one row per day.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: qualtrics__distribution
      description: Qualtrics distributions enriched with owner, mailing list, parent subject, and aggregated delivery/response metrics
      grain: One row per distribution_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__user
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_mailing_list
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution_contact
      business_logic: 'Base: - Start from staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution as the base (one row per distribution_id). Enrichments: - Owner details: left join staging.stg_qualtrics__user on owner_user_id = user_id to add owner_email, owner_first_name, owner_last_name. - Parent subject: self-join on parent_distribution_id = distribution_id to add parent_distribution_header_subject from the parent row. - Mailing list name: left join staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_mailing_list on recipient_mailing_list_id = mailing_list_id to add recipient_mailing_list_name. Distribution-contact metrics: - Build distribution_contact from staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution_contact and derive per contact: - time_to_open_in_seconds: seconds between sent_at and opened_at. - time_to_start_in_seconds: seconds between sent_at and response_started_at. - time_to_complete_in_seconds: seconds between sent_at and response_completed_at. - Durations are NULL if either endpoint is NULL; units are seconds. - Aggregate per distribution_id: - Status counts: for each status value (pending, success, error, opened, complaint, skipped, blocked, failure, unknown, softbounce, hardbounce, surveystarted, surveypartiallyfinished, surveyfinished, surveyscreenedout, sessionexpired), count contact records whose lowercase status equals the value; NULL and non-matching statuses are excluded. - Contact totals: number of unique contact_ids; and unique contact_ids with sent_at/opened_at/response_started_at/response_completed_at present. - First/last timestamps: earliest and latest of sent_at, opened_at, and response_completed_at across contacts; null if no non-null values. - Averages: mean of non-null time_to_open/start/complete durations; null if no non-null values. - Median metrics: - For each duration (open/start/complete), compute the continuous median (50th percentile) across non-null values, using linear interpolation when needed. Final projection: - Select all base columns and add enrichment/metric columns. - Coalesce only the numeric counts (status counts and distinct contact counts) to 0; timestamps, averages, and medians may remain NULL. Output: - One row per distribution_id from the base, with left-join semantics for enrichments and metrics.'

references.name: staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution
references.line_text: business_logic: 'Base: - Start from staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution as the base (one row per distribution_id). Enrichments: - Owner details: left join staging.stg_qualtrics__user on owner_user_id = user_id to add owner_email, owner_first_name, owner_last_name. - Parent subject: self-join on parent_distribution_id = distribution_id to add parent_distribution_header_subject from the parent row. - Mailing list name: left join staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_mailing_list on recipient_mailing_list_id = mailing_list_id to add recipient_mailing_list_name. Distribution-contact metrics: - Build distribution_contact from staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution_contact and derive per contact: - time_to_open_in_seconds: seconds between sent_at and opened_at. - time_to_start_in_seconds: seconds between sent_at and response_started_at. - time_to_complete_in_seconds: seconds between sent_at and response_completed_at. - Durations are NULL if either endpoint is NULL; units are seconds. - Aggregate per distribution_id: - Status counts: for each status value (pending, success, error, opened, complaint, skipped, blocked, failure, unknown, softbounce, hardbounce, surveystarted, surveypartiallyfinished, surveyfinished, surveyscreenedout, sessionexpired), count contact records whose lowercase status equals the value; NULL and non-matching statuses are excluded. - Contact totals: number of unique contact_ids; and unique contact_ids with sent_at/opened_at/response_started_at/response_completed_at present. - First/last timestamps: earliest and latest of sent_at, opened_at, and response_completed_at across contacts; null if no non-null values. - Averages: mean of non-null time_to_open/start/complete durations; null if no non-null values. - Median metrics: - For each duration (open/start/complete), compute the continuous median (50th percentile) across non-null values, using linear interpolation when needed. Final projection: - Select all base columns and add enrichment/metric columns. - Coalesce only the numeric counts (status counts and distinct contact counts) to 0; timestamps, averages, and medians may remain NULL. Output: - One row per distribution_id from the base, with left-join semantics for enrichments and metrics.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: qualtrics__response
      description: Response-level table enriched with survey, question, option, embedded data, and contact rollups
      grain: One row per question_response_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__responses
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__question_option
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__question
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey_embedded_data
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__contacts
      business_logic: '- Start with all rows from intermediate.int_qualtrics__responses; the base grain is one row per question_response_id. - Build rollup_contacts by grouping intermediate.int_qualtrics__contacts on email and aggregating: - first_name, last_name, email_domain, language, external_data_reference: take the maximum value per email, ignoring NULLs; for strings, this is the highest lexicographic value; return NULL if all values are NULL. - is_xm_directory_contact, is_research_core_contact: logical OR per email; TRUE if any TRUE, FALSE if all FALSE and at least one non-NULL, NULL if all values are NULL. - Left join intermediate.int_qualtrics__question on matching survey_id, question_id, and sub_question_key. - Left join staging.stg_qualtrics__question_option on matching survey_id and question_id, comparing the option keys as strings. - Left join staging.stg_qualtrics__survey on survey_id. - Left join intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey_embedded_data on survey_response_id equals response_id. - Left join rollup_contacts on recipient_email equals email. - Output includes all base response columns plus the joined fields. - All joins are LEFT; unmatched joins produce NULLs. No filtering or sorting is applied. No deduplication is performed; non-unique join keys can duplicate base rows. survey_response_recorded_at is not cast and remains text.'
      columns:
      - name: question_response_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique identifier for the question-level response; primary grain key
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: survey_response_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Response-level identifier used to join embedded data
      - name: survey_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey identifier used to join survey and question attributes
      - name: question_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Question identifier used to join question and option attributes
      - name: question_text
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Question text from the base response
      - name: sub_question_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Sub-question key used in the question join
      - name: sub_question_text
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Numeric sub-question label from the base response
      - name: question_option_key
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Selected option key from the base response; matched to option by comparing keys as strings
      - name: value
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Numeric response value from the base response
      - name: response_text
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Text response value from the base response
      - name: loop_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Loop iteration identifier from the base response
      - name: distribution_channel
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Distribution channel of the response
      - name: survey_response_status
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Flag indicating the response status
      - name: survey_progress
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of survey completed
      - name: duration_in_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total response duration in seconds
      - name: is_finished_with_survey
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Indicates whether the respondent finished the survey
      - name: survey_finished_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp when the survey was finished
      - name: survey_response_last_modified_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp when the response was last modified
      - name: survey_response_recorded_at
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Recorded-at value retained as text
      - name: survey_response_started_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp when the response started
      - name: recipient_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Recipient email used to join rollup_contacts
      - name: recipient_first_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Recipient first name from the base response
      - name: recipient_last_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Recipient last name from the base response
      - name: user_language
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Respondent language from the base response
      - name: ip_address
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: IP address of the respondent
      - name: location_latitude
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Latitude of respondent location
      - name: location_longitude
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Longitude of respondent location
      - name: recode_value
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Option recode value from question_option joined on survey_id and question_id with option keys matched as strings
      - name: question_option_text
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Option text from question_option joined on survey_id and question_id with option keys matched as strings
      - name: first_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact first name aggregated as the maximum value per email; NULL if all values are NULL
      - name: last_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact last name aggregated as the maximum value per email; NULL if all values are NULL
      - name: email_domain
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact email domain aggregated as the maximum value per email; NULL if all values are NULL
      - name: contact_language
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact language aggregated as the maximum value per email; NULL if all values are NULL
      - name: contact_external_data_reference
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: External data reference aggregated as the maximum value per email; NULL if all values are NULL
      - name: is_xm_directory_contact
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Aggregated as logical OR across contacts by email; TRUE if any TRUE, FALSE if all FALSE with at least one non-NULL, NULL if all NULL
      - name: is_research_core_contact
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Aggregated as logical OR across contacts by email; TRUE if any TRUE, FALSE if all FALSE with at least one non-NULL, NULL if all NULL
      - name: embedded_data
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Embedded data JSON/text joined on survey_response_id equals response_id
      - name: survey_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey name joined on survey_id
      - name: survey_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey status joined on survey_id
      - name: project_category
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey project category joined on survey_id
      - name: project_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey project type joined on survey_id
      - name: brand_base_url
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Brand base URL joined on survey_id
      - name: question_description
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Question description joined on survey_id, question_id, and sub_question_key
      - name: question_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Question type joined on survey_id, question_id, and sub_question_key
      - name: block_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Block ID joined on survey_id, question_id, and sub_question_key
      - name: block_description
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Block description joined on survey_id, question_id, and sub_question_key
      - name: block_question_randomization
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Question randomization setting from the question join
      - name: block_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Block type from the question join
      - name: block_visibility
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Block visibility setting from the question join
      - name: validation_setting_force_response
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Force response validation setting from the question join
      - name: validation_setting_force_response_type
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Force response validation type from the question join
      - name: validation_setting_type
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Validation setting type from the question join

No filtering or sorting is applied. No deduplication is performed; non-unique join keys can duplicate base rows. survey_response_recorded_at is not cast and remains text.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: qualtrics__survey
      description: Survey-level rollup of base survey attributes joined with question counts, response aggregates, medians, and distribution-channel counts
      grain: One row per survey_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__question
      business_logic: '- Start with all columns from intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey as the base survey record; output one row per survey_id. - Questions: from staging.stg_qualtrics__question, group by survey_id and count distinct question_id as count_questions; left join to the base; if no matches, set count_questions to 0. - Response aggregates: from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response, group by survey_id and compute: - Averages: avg_response_duration_in_seconds from duration_in_seconds and avg_survey_progress_pct from progress, both over non-null values; if no contributing rows, leave as NULL. - Totals: count_survey_responses as distinct response_id; count_completed_survey_responses as distinct response_id where the response is marked finished. - 30-day window: count_survey_responses_30d and count_completed_survey_responses_30d include responses whose recorded_date can be parsed to a timestamp and falls within the last 30 calendar days relative to query time, with the boundary included; the completed variant also requires finished responses; rows with unparseable recorded_date are excluded from these 30-day counts. - Channel buckets (distinct response_id): anonymous (''anonymous''), social media (''social''), personal link (''gl''), QR code (''qr''), email (''email''), and SMS (''smsinvite''); for each, also compute a completed version requiring finished responses. Uncategorized buckets include responses whose channel is a non-null value not in the listed set; responses with NULL channel are excluded from all channel buckets, including uncategorized. - Medians: per survey_id, compute the median (50th percentile) of duration_in_seconds and of progress over non-null values; if no contributing rows, leave as NULL. - Join: left join question, response aggregates, and medians to the base by survey_id. Coalesce all count metrics to 0; averages and medians remain NULL when no data. All counts use distinct response_id or question_id.'
      columns:
      - name: survey_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary key from the base survey; exactly one output row per survey_id

        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey display name passed through from intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey

      - name: default_scoring_category

      - name: division_id

        description: Creator Qualtrics user ID passed through from intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey
      - name: owner_user_id

      - name: project_category

        description: Project category passed through from intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey

        description: Project type passed through from intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey

      - name: registry_version

        description: Registry version number passed through from intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey
      - name: schema_version
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Schema version number passed through from intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey
      - name: scoring_summary_after_questions
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Flag indicating scoring summary after questions passed through from intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey

      - name: version_id

        description: Distinct questions per survey; set to 0 when no questions are found
      - name: avg_response_duration_in_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average response duration over non-null values; seconds; NULL when no qualifying responses
      - name: median_response_duration_in_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Median (50th percentile) of response duration over non-null values; seconds; NULL when no qualifying responses
      - name: avg_survey_progress_pct

      - name: median_survey_progress_pct

        description: Median (50th percentile) of response progress over non-null values; percentage (0–100); NULL when no qualifying responses
      - name: count_survey_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct responses per survey; set to 0 when none
      - name: count_completed_survey_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct finished responses per survey; set to 0 when none
      - name: count_survey_responses_30d

        description: Distinct responses recorded in the last 30 days (inclusive) based on a parsable recorded_date; set to 0 when none; unparseable dates are excluded
      - name: count_completed_survey_responses_30d
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct finished responses recorded in the last 30 days (inclusive) based on a parsable recorded_date; set to 0 when none
      - name: count_anonymous_survey_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct responses with channel 'anonymous'; set to 0 when none
      - name: count_anonymous_completed_survey_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct finished responses with channel 'anonymous'; set to 0 when none

        data_type: BIGINT

      - name: count_personal_link_survey_responses

references.name: intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey
references.line_text: business_logic: '- Start with all columns from intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey as the base survey record; output one row per survey_id. - Questions: from staging.stg_qualtrics__question, group by survey_id and count distinct question_id as count_questions; left join to the base; if no matches, set count_questions to 0. - Response aggregates: from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response, group by survey_id and compute: - Averages: avg_response_duration_in_seconds from duration_in_seconds and avg_survey_progress_pct from progress, both over non-null values; if no contributing rows, leave as NULL. - Totals: count_survey_responses as distinct response_id; count_completed_survey_responses as distinct response_id where the response is marked finished. - 30-day window: count_survey_responses_30d and count_completed_survey_responses_30d include responses whose recorded_date can be parsed to a timestamp and falls within the last 30 calendar days relative to query time, with the boundary included; the completed variant also requires finished responses; rows with unparseable recorded_date are excluded from these 30-day counts. - Channel buckets (distinct response_id): anonymous (''anonymous''), social media (''social''), personal link (''gl''), QR code (''qr''), email (''email''), and SMS (''smsinvite''); for each, also compute a completed version requiring finished responses. Uncategorized buckets include responses whose channel is a non-null value not in the listed set; responses with NULL channel are excluded from all channel buckets, including uncategorized. - Medians: per survey_id, compute the median (50th percentile) of duration_in_seconds and of progress over non-null values; if no contributing rows, leave as NULL. - Join: left join question, response aggregates, and medians to the base by survey_id. Coalesce all count metrics to 0; averages and medians remain NULL when no data. All counts use distinct response_id or question_id.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: qualtrics__survey_analytics
      description: Survey-level performance and quality metrics joined to a per-survey quality summary, restricted to surveys with total_responses > 0.
      grain: One row per survey_id with total_responses > 0
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey_performance
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__response_quality
      business_logic: '- Load survey_performance with survey_id, survey_name, survey_status, total_responses, completed_responses, completion_rate, and avg_completion_time_seconds. - Load response_quality with survey_id, response_id, include_in_analysis, quality_score, and overall_quality_rating. - Build a quality_summary per survey_id: - total_assessed_responses = number of distinct response_id values. - high_quality_responses = number of responses where include_in_analysis is true; false or null are not counted. - avg_quality_score = average of quality_score values; records with null quality_score are ignored; no rounding. - excellent_responses = number of responses where overall_quality_rating equals "High Quality" (exact string match). - Left join survey_performance to quality_summary by survey_id. - When quality_summary is missing, set avg_quality_score, high_quality_responses, and excellent_responses to 0; if avg_quality_score is null, use 0. - Compute quality_adjusted_completion_rate: - If total_responses > 0 and total_assessed_responses > 0, multiply completion_rate by the fraction high_quality_responses / total_responses (fractional division; no truncation); otherwise use completion_rate; if completion_rate is null, the result is null. - Assign performance_tier using inclusive thresholds: - High Performer when completion_rate ≥ 0.8 and avg_quality_score (using 0 when missing) ≥ 80. - Good Performer when completion_rate ≥ 0.6 and avg_quality_score (using 0 when missing) ≥ 60. - Average Performer when completion_rate ≥ 0.4. - Otherwise Needs Improvement. - Compute roi_score as completion_rate * 60 plus avg_quality_score (using 0 when missing) * 0.4; if completion_rate is null, roi_score is null; no rounding. - Set analysis_date to the current timestamp (same value for all rows in a run). - Filter out surveys where total_responses ≤ 0 or total_responses is null. - Order the final output by roi_score descending.'
      columns:
      - name: survey_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique survey identifier and join key; one output row per survey_id after filtering to total_responses > 0.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: survey_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Survey name from survey_performance; passed through with nulls preserved.
      - name: survey_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current survey status from survey_performance; passed through with nulls preserved.
      - name: total_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total responses from survey_performance; strictly greater than 0 in the output due to final filter.
      - name: completed_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Completed response count from survey_performance; passed through with nulls preserved.
      - name: completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completion rate from survey_performance used in adjustments, tiering, and ROI; passed through with nulls preserved.
      - name: avg_completion_time_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average completion time in seconds from survey_performance; passed through without rounding; nulls preserved.
      - name: avg_quality_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of quality_score per survey ignoring nulls; uses 0 when no matching quality_summary or the average is null.
      - name: high_quality_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of responses where include_in_analysis is true; uses 0 when no matching quality_summary; no de-dup beyond distinct response counting in total_assessed_responses.
      - name: excellent_responses
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of responses where overall_quality_rating equals 'High Quality'; uses 0 when no matching quality_summary; exact string match; no de-duplication.
      - name: quality_adjusted_completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: If total_responses > 0 and total_assessed_responses > 0, completion_rate multiplied by high_quality_responses divided by total_responses (fractional division); otherwise completion_rate; null when completion_rate is null; no rounding.
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Classification: High Performer, Good Performer, Average Performer, or Needs Improvement based on inclusive completion_rate thresholds and avg_quality_score using 0 when missing.'
      - name: roi_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Score computed as completion_rate * 60 plus avg_quality_score (using 0 when missing) * 0.4; null when completion_rate is null; no rounding.
      - name: analysis_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution timestamp from current_timestamp; identical across rows within a run and not null.

constant_nonnull_columns.value_representation: DuckDB CAST AS VARCHAR, exact, no normalization

blocks.original_text:
- name: qualtrics__user_cohort_analysis
      description: 'Monthly user cohort metrics from Qualtrics responses: cohort size, per-user averages, value-tier counts, and a 0–100 health score'
      grain: One row per cohort_month
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
      business_logic: 'Build cohorts from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response: - Keep only records with recorded_date present. - Define user_identifier: use recipient_email when available; otherwise use the literal prefix "anonymous_" followed by response_id. - Per user_identifier: - first_response_date: the earliest timestamp parsed from recorded_date. - cohort_month: the first calendar day of the month of first_response_date. - total_responses: count of distinct response_id. - completed_responses: count of distinct response_id where is_finished is true (null/false excluded). - completion_rate (percent): if total_responses > 0, completed_responses / total_responses × 100; otherwise 0. Use decimal division. - user_value_tier by total_responses: ≥20 Power User; ≥10 High Value; ≥5 Medium Value; ≥2 Low Value; else One-time User. Aggregate by cohort_month: - cohort_size: distinct users in the cohort. - avg_responses_per_user: average of per-user total_responses. - avg_completion_rate: average of per-user completion_rate (percent). - power_users/high_value_users/medium_value_users/low_value_users/one_time_users: counts of users in each tier. - cohort_health_score: 0.6 × avg_completion_rate + 40 × (count of Power or High Value users ÷ cohort_size). Expected range 0–100. Finalize: - Exclude cohorts where cohort_size = 0. - Return one row per cohort_month; sorted descending by cohort_month (sorting does not affect values).'
      columns:
      - name: cohort_month
        data_type: DATE
        description: First day of the month of each user's first response; cohort grouping key.
      - name: cohort_size
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of distinct users in the cohort_month.
      - name: avg_responses_per_user
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean per-user count of distinct responses within the cohort.
      - name: avg_completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean per-user completion rate in percent, where per-user rate is completed distinct responses divided by total distinct responses times 100.
      - name: power_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses ≥ 20 in the cohort.
      - name: high_value_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses ≥ 10 and < 20 in the cohort.
      - name: medium_value_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses ≥ 5 and < 10 in the cohort.
      - name: low_value_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses ≥ 2 and < 5 in the cohort.
      - name: one_time_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses = 1 in the cohort.
      - name: cohort_health_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: '0–100 score: 0.6×avg_completion_rate + 40×(share of Power or High Value users in the cohort).'

constant_nonnull_columns.value_representation: DuckDB CAST AS VARCHAR, exact, no normalization

blocks.original_text:
- name: stg_qualtrics__directory_contact
      description: "Cleaned and validated Qualtrics directory contact records including email normalization, phone digitization, and unsubscribe tracking"
      source_table: "raw.directory_contact"
      primary_key: ["contact_id"]
      columns:
        - name: contact_id
          data_type: VARCHAR
          constraints: [not_null, unique]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "contact_id IS NOT NULL"
              on_failure: delete_row
        - name: created_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
        - name: directory_id
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: unsubscribed_from_directory_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
        - name: is_unsubscribed_from_directory
          data_type: BOOLEAN
        - name: email
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "email IS NULL OR email = LOWER(TRIM(email))"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "email IS NULL OR email ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$'"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: email_domain
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "email_domain IS NULL OR email_domain = LOWER(TRIM(email_domain))"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: ext_ref
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "ext_ref IS NULL OR LENGTH(TRIM(ext_ref)) = LENGTH(ext_ref)"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: first_name
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "first_name IS NULL OR LENGTH(TRIM(first_name)) = LENGTH(first_name)"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: last_name
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "last_name IS NULL OR LENGTH(TRIM(last_name)) = LENGTH(last_name)"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: phone
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "phone IS NULL OR REGEXP_REPLACE(phone, '[^0-9]', '', 'g') = phone"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "phone IS NULL OR LENGTH(phone) >= 5"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: language
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "language IS NULL OR LENGTH(TRIM(language)) = LENGTH(language)"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: last_modified_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "last_modified_at IS NULL OR last_modified_at >= created_at"
              on_failure: warn_and_continue

      source_table: "raw.survey_response"

      columns:
        - name: response_id
          data_type: VARCHAR
          constraints: [not_null, unique]
        - name: survey_id
          data_type: VARCHAR

        - name: is_finished
          data_type: BOOLEAN
          constraints: [not_null]
        - name: progress
          data_type: DOUBLE
        - name: duration_in_seconds
          data_type: DOUBLE
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "duration_in_seconds IS NULL OR duration_in_seconds >= 0"
              on_failure: nullify_field
              description: "Duration cannot be negative"
            - rule: "duration_in_seconds IS NULL OR duration_in_seconds <= 86400"
              on_failure: warn_and_continue
              description: "Duration over 24 hours is suspicious but not invalid"
        - name: recorded_date
          data_type: VARCHAR
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "recorded_date IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(TRIM(recorded_date)) > 0"
              on_failure: delete_row
              description: "Response date must exist"
        - name: started_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
        - name: finished_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
        - name: recipient_email
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "recipient_email IS NULL OR recipient_email = LOWER(TRIM(recipient_email))"
              on_failure: correct
              description: "Normalize email to lowercase and remove whitespace"
            - rule: "recipient_email IS NULL OR recipient_email ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$'"
              on_failure: nullify_field
              description: "Email must be valid format or null for anonymous responses"

        - name: recipient_last_name

        - name: distribution_channel

        - name: ip_address

        - name: last_modified_at

        - name: location_latitude

        - name: location_longitude
